items.title: #NSTviral: Motorcyclist's roadside rescue with cat sparks debate
items.summary: Ahmad Mukhsein Mukhtar KUALA LUMPUR: An unusual roadside rescue involving a motorcyclist, a cat and a stranded food delivery rider has captured the attention of Malaysians online. The 22-second clip, posted on TikTok by user @_mses, shows the motorcyclist travelling along a highway in the capital with a cat clinging to him. "The cat is so cute," user @m1noo wrote.

items.title: Pakatan leaders vow collective responsibility for Negeri Sembilan loss, pledge continued commitment to constituents
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — All Pakatan Harapan (PH) leaders will take collective responsibility for the coalition’s defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said last night. He said the coalition’s leadership, from the highest level down to the grassroots, would shoulder responsibility collectively, stressing that no individual, group, community or faction would be singled out for blame. According to unofficial results, PH has garnered 11 of 36 seats it contested in the election, while Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured 18 and seven seats respectively.

items.title: Zahid: BN submits three names for Negeri Sembilan menteri besar post
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said that the coalition has submitted three names of candidates for the position of Menteri Besar to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. The Umno president said he delivered the official letter during an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap here tonight. Earlier, Tuanku Muhriz granted an audience to Ahmad Zahid at approximately 10 pm.

items.title: Nga: Chennah, Repah losses a bitter lesson for DAP
items.summary: SEREMBAN: DAP accepts the outcome of the Negri Sembilan state election with an open heart and respects the mandate delivered by voters, says party deputy chairman Datuk Seri Nga Kor Ming. Although the result fell short of Pakatan Harapan's (PH) expectations, Nga said the coalition accepted the outcome and would conduct a thorough post-mortem to address its shortcomings. However, PH will not lose heart.

items.title: PM Anwar pledges continued cooperation, federal support for Negeri Sembilan government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the federal government will continue to extend its support and cooperation to the new Negeri Sembilan state government for the well-being and prosperity of the state and its people. Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) would form the Negeri Sembilan state government after securing a two-thirds majority win in the state polls. The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly has 36 seats.

items.title: Zahid: Don't pressure Aminuddin to vacate MB's official residence
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun should not be pressured to vacate the official Menteri Besar's residence, recalling that similar pressure was placed on Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan in 2023. Instead, Zahid said there should be humanity among political leaders. He said this when met by reporters outside Istana Hinggap Negri Sembilan here last night.

items.title: Saleswoman loses RM290,000 to investment scam, fake recovery agent
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 61-year-old supermarket saleswoman lost RM290,910 after falling victim to an online investment scheme and a scammer posing as an officer promising to recover her money. He said the victim was attracted by low-capital offers promising high returns in a short period, leading her to make initial capital payments and several additional transactions to redeem her alleged profits. Azli said the victim, believing the claims, made 57 transactions to 16 different bank accounts between June 14 and July 31.

items.title: Brazilian man stabs three to death at factory, later found dead
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: A Brazilian man who fatally stabbed three people at a factory in Sao Paulo was later found dead after his arrest. The 33-year-old man entered his workplace on Saturday before stabbing three people, aged 39 to 54, AFP reported. According to local media, the man, a forklift operator, had gone to the factory on his day off to kill two people.

items.title: N9 polls: Siti Nur Umaira youngest winner, Mohamad Hasan oldest
items.summary: Siti Nur Umaira, the Rasah UMNO Puteri division chief, secured 14,209 votes to win the seat with a majority of 5,279 votes, defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Ahmad Faez Abdul Razak (8,930 votes) and Bersatu incumbent Mohamad Hanifah Abu Baker (1,985 votes). Meanwhile, Mohamad retained the Rantau state seat by securing 19,050 votes to defeat PH's Dr Azizul Hakim Mahdi (7,032 votes) in a straight fight. He polled 32,004 votes in a three-cornered fight, defeating PH's Ahmad Shahir Mohd Shah (15,045 votes) and Bersatu's Mohd Nazree Mohd Yunus (2,205 votes).

items.title: Capital One says it closed Trump Organisation's accounts after anti-money laundering probe
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Capital One Financial hit back on Friday against a lawsuit over its decision to close the Trump Organisation's bank accounts years ago, stating that it did so after a review by anti-money laundering experts. The Trump Organisation and Capital One did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Capital One has never accused the Trump Organisation of illegal money laundering.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill at least four in Gaza despite Trump announcing breakthrough
items.summary: CAIRO: Israeli airstrikes continued in Gaza for a second straight day on Sunday, killing at least four Palestinians, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year's Gaza ceasefire agreement. Palestinian health officials said Israeli warplanes carried out separate strikes in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah. Trump said on Thursday there had been a breakthrough after Hamas agreed to disarm under a US-backed initiative to implement the ceasefire agreement reached last year in Egypt.

items.title: Selangor to review stray animal management SOPs across all local authorities
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government will review the standard operating procedures (SOPs) for managing stray animals across all local authorities to ensure enforcement operations are carried out more effectively, safely and humanely. Ng said the state government also expressed its appreciation for the advice of Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who emphasised the importance of compassion towards animals and the principle that no one is above the law. "Such values will continue to guide the state government's policies and decisions," he said.

items.title: Expert urges KLIA security, aviation safety review after Malaysia Airlines pilot's drug arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia over a drug smuggling attempt has exposed weaknesses in both aviation safety oversight and airport security systems at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), an aviation expert said. Associate Professor Dr Mohd Harridon Mohamed Suffian said the incident should prompt a comprehensive review of drug detection programmes and security screening procedures for airline staff at KLIA. Malaysia Airlines on Friday said it was conducting an internal review.

items.title: CAAM probes security procedures after Malaysia Airlines pilot's drug arrest [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) is investigating whether all aviation security procedures were followed after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling. CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the incident, which is under investigation by Indonesian authorities, would also be assessed from a regulatory perspective, including the airline's compliance with aviation security requirements and the airport operator's screening processes before the pilot departed Malaysia. "Like all other persons entering the Security Restricted Area, aircrew are required to undergo security screening before being granted access.

items.title: Seismic shift in Malaysian politics as BN-Perikatan ousts Pakatan heavyweights in Negeri Sembilan poll
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Negeri Sembilan woke up to a transformed political landscape this morning after voters decisively handed control of the state to a Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) alliance. The outcome effectively toppled the Pakatan Harapan (PH) administration and unseated two of the coalition’s most powerful figures: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun. Unofficial data from the Election Commission (EC) indicated that BN emerged as the largest bloc with 18 seats, while PN took seven.

items.title: Iran threatens to strike other nations' energy fields if US launches fresh attacks
items.summary: CAIRO: Iran warned this weekend against any "adventurous action" by the US and said it would retaliate decisively if American forces follow through on President Donald Trump's threats of fresh attacks on Iranian targets. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi's comments in separate phone calls on Saturday with senior Turkish, Pakistani and Saudi officials came just hours after Kuwait's army said it destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran against several vital facilities. Speaking to Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Araqchi said Iran would respond decisively to any "aggression" and discussed the consequences of "destabilising actions" by the US, as well as prospects for heightened regional insecurity, according to Araqchi's Telegram account.

items.title: 13 dead after small tourist plane crashes in Peru
items.summary: LIMA: A small plane carrying foreign tourists to view Peru's famed Nazca Lines archaeological site crashed on Saturday, killing all 13 people on board, police said. "We have information that 11 passengers and two crew members have died," Police Major Jorge Andrade told reporters at the crash site. RPP radio reported that seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards were killed.

items.title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja, team killed in Pakistan avalanche
items.summary: SKARDU: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were killed in an avalanche in Pakistan during an ascent of one of the world's highest mountains, his expedition company said on Saturday, as rescuers tackled treacherous conditions to recover their bodies. The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by Purja, a 43-year-old British-Nepali climber, on Broad Peak in northern Pakistan. "It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," Purja's company, Elite Expeditions, said on social media.

items.title: Zahid submits three names to Negri Sembilan palace for MB post
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has submitted three names to the Negri Sembilan palace for consideration as the state's next Menteri Besar. Zahid said the final decision rests entirely with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, who has the prerogative to appoint one of the candidates. Zahid said all three candidates submitted were from BN.

items.title: EC confirms BN victory with 18 seats in Negri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Election Commission (EC) has officially announced that BN won 18 seats in the 16th Negri Sembilan election. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said PH secured 12 seats, while PN won seven. He said Bersatu, Barisan Jemaah Islamiah Se-Malaysia (Berjasa), Parti Orang Asli Malaysia (Asli), Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) and four Independent candidates failed to win any seats.

items.title: Chow: No need for Loke to step down immediately
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: There is no immediate need for Anthony Loke to step down as Negri Sembilan DAP chairman following the party's defeat in the state election, says Chow Kon Yeow. Chow, a DAP central executive committee member, said Loke should be given time to regroup and rally party members before making any decision on his position, according to FMT. Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, had said he would consider stepping down as the party's Negri Sembilan chairman after losing the Chennah seat in the Aug 1 state election.

items.title: Wan Saiful calls on Bersatu members to abandon 'sinking ship' after Negri results
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Wawasan vice-president Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan has called on Bersatu members to abandon the party and join Wawasan. Wan Saiful said the Negri Sembilan election results had made clear that Bersatu was no longer politically relevant. Wan Saiful, who said he had personally represented Perikatan Nasional (PN) in a series of meetings with Barisan Nasional (BN) during the campaign, congratulated BN on winning 18 state seats and PN on claiming seven.

items.title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja, team killed in Pakistan avalanche
items.summary: SKARDU: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were all killed by an avalanche in Pakistan during an ascent of one of the world's highest mountains, his expedition company said on Saturday, as rescuers tackled treacherous conditions to recover their bodies. The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by Purja, a 43-year-old British-Nepali climber, on Broad Peak in northern Pakistan. "It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," Purja's company Elite Expeditions said on social media.

items.title: Bersatu to explore coalition with moderate parties after Negri polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu said it will discuss forming a coalition with moderate and progressive parties to inject fresh energy into the country's democracy following its solo outing in the Negri Sembilan election. In a statement, the party said the move would be pursued "for a brighter future". "Bersatu will discuss the formation of a coalition of moderate and progressive parties to revitalise democracy in the country for a brighter future," it said.

items.title: Caretaker MB Aminuddin loses Linggi by nearly 3,000 votes in Negri Sembilan polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Caretaker Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun suffered a crushing defeat in the Linggi state seat, losing to Barisan Nasional's Mohd Faizal Ramli by a majority of 2,976 votes. Aminuddin, who is also state Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, fell heavily in a seat he had chosen to contest over his traditional Sikamat stronghold, where he had served as assemblyman for four consecutive terms. BN's retention of Linggi formed part of a sweeping night for the coalition, which claimed 18 of the 36 seats in the Negri Sembilan state assembly, with BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) together surpassing the two-thirds majority threshold with 25 seats combined.

items.title: Anwar congratulates BN on Negri win, pledges federal support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Barisan Nasional (BN) on its victory in the Negri Sembilan election. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, pledged that the federal government would continue to support the new state government for the welfare and prosperity of the state and its people. He also expressed his appreciation to the people of Negri Sembilan for placing their trust in PH and caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun over the past eight years.

items.title: When a rumour sparked a rush for Europe
items.summary: AFP images showed people swimming around Ceuta's frontier fence and others clambering over barbed wire to reach European soil, as Moroccan riot police fired tear gas and water cannon at crowds after an apparent breakdown of border controls. An AFP journalist on the scene witnessed the arrest of around 30 young people. Zahra was eventually turned away at the Moroccan border town of Fnideq, but Ceuta's regional president said some 60,000 people had successfully entered the tiny territory of just 80,000 residents.

items.title: Hadi says success in Negri will spark a 'bigger wave of change'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Datuk Seri Abdul Hadi Awang expressed his appreciation to voters in Negri Sembilan for placing their trust in Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the state election. In a statement, he said the result was a clear signal that the people had accepted efforts towards unity among Muslims rooted in justice, welfare and harmony within a plural society. His statement follows today's state election, in which BN and PN unofficially secured 25 of the 36 seats contested, surpassing the two-thirds majority needed to form the state government.

items.title: NS polls: Loke, Aminuddin among biggest casualties as BN wins 18 seats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: BN swept to 18 seats in the 36-seat Negri Sembilan state assembly, delivering a crushing blow to PH as DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun were among its biggest casualties, while BN and PN combined to secure a two-thirds majority. PN won seven seats — Klawang, Serting, Sikamat, Ampangan, Paroi, Bagan Pinang and Gemas — with the latter marking Parti Wawasan's first-ever state seat victory. Together, BN and PN secured 25 of the 36 seats in the Negri Sembilan state assembly, surpassing the 24-seat threshold required for a two-thirds majority.

items.title: AI is rewriting Asia's air cargo story
items.summary: The global race to build artificial intelligence is redrawing Asia's air cargo map, prompting airlines to redesign networks around growing semiconductor manufacturing hubs as cross-border ecommerce loses momentum. Cargo revenue surged 46 per cent in the second quarter to 1.54 trillion won (US$1.07 billion), driven by AI chips, server racks and data centre infrastructure that the airline said had replaced e-commerce shipments from China as its primary growth engine. Advanced high-tech cargo "has rapidly expanded as a core growth driver", said Jaedong Eum, executive vice-president and head of Korean Air's cargo business.

items.title: NST Leader: Tabung Haji and the price of greed
items.summary: When greed, poor governance and financial mismanagement come together, they can bring down mighty institutions. They almost did it to Tabung Haji, which manages billions of ringgit in Muslim depositors' funds. Greed, poor governance and financial mismanagement are Malaysian diseases of old.

items.title: Negri victory strengthens case for BN-PN cooperation in Melaka, say analysts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: BN and PN should maintain their electoral cooperation in Melaka following their sweep in the Negri Sembilan election, but should avoid formalising the arrangement, political analysts said. He said Melaka would serve as the next test of whether the BN-PN formula used in Johor and the Negri Sembilan election could become a broader political trend. she said.

items.title: Police hunt motorcyclist after roadside brawl at Port Klang junction goes viral
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: South Klang police are hunting an unidentified motorcyclist following a roadside brawl at the junction of Jalan Kastam that was captured on video and has since gone viral on social media. The incident took place at around 3.30pm on July 29, when a 30-year-old local male car driver came to blows with the motorcyclist at the junction, district police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey said in a statement today. Police urged members of the public with any information related to the case to come forward and assist with investigations by contacting investigating officer Inspector Mohd Shauqhi Abdul Shukor at 011-51691730, the South Klang police operations room at 03-33762222, or the nearest police station.

items.title: Pakatan blames ‘racial politics’ after defeat to BN-Perikatan pact in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has attributed its dismal performance in today’s Negeri Sembilan state election to "racial and identity politics," cautioning that such polarising tactics threaten to fracture the state’s multi-ethnic social fabric. The coalition’s Election Department confirmed that PH unofficially won in only 11 of the 36 seats contested. “This state election witnessed an extraordinary campaign of racial politics based almost entirely on identity, which has the potential to sow division within society and the state.

items.title: Zahid: BN and PN will partner to establish Negeri Sembilan administration
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will form the new Negeri Sembilan government after securing a two-thirds majority in today’s state election, based on unofficial results. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the unofficial results showed BN had won 18 seats while PN secured seven, giving the two coalitions a combined majority to form the state administration. Ahmad Zahid said the new state government will be built on an understanding between BN and PN, while upholding the mandate given by the people.

items.title: A ride cut short: Homeward-bound varsity student dies on highway after RXZ 8.0 gathering in Gong Badak
items.summary: DUNGUN, Aug 1 — A private university student was killed when the motorcycle he was riding skidded at Kilometre 354 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), near here, today. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said 22-year-old Muhammad Bakhtiar Mazlan, from Parit Raja, Batu Pahat, Johor, was confirmed dead at the scene due to severe head injuries. He said police received a call from members of the public regarding the incident involving a Honda Vario motorcycle at about 3pm.

items.title: Economy Ministry eyes pilot project as Malaysia’s ageing population threatens fiscal and care pressures
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 1 — The Economy Ministry is identifying a pilot project to address challenges arising from Malaysia’s ageing population, with plans to roll it out next year. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the ageing agenda had been designated as a key pillar under the 13th Malaysia Plan. He said planning for the second rolling plan for next year’s development expenditure would be structured to cover all segments, including initiatives to address population ageing.

items.title: Myvi and Saga collide near Kelantan school, 80-year-old woman dies, four others seriously injured
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 1 — An 80-year-old woman was killed while four others, including two drivers, were seriously injured in a two-car collision near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Kedai Piah, Ketereh, here this afternoon. Ketereh Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Nazri Taib said firefighters arrived at the scene four minutes after receiving an emergency call at 3.25pm. “Four other victims aged between nine and 38, including both drivers, suffered serious injuries,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Penang Port marks 70 years by giving back to those in need
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 1 — The Penang Port Commission (SPPP) reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that the benefits of port development reach all segments of society, particularly those in need, in line with the Malaysia Madani aspirations. Its chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said SPPP’s role over the past 70 years had extended beyond advancing the port sector to supporting community well-being through various welfare initiatives. “Today, under the spirit of Madani, we reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that the benefits of development reach all segments of society, especially those in need,” he said at a tea reception held in conjunction with SPPP’s 70th anniversary celebration and the launch of the Penang Port 2026 National Month Celebration here today.

items.title: A Paka R&R special? Terengganu police nab trio over alleged open sale of ketum water, one suspect just 16
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 1 — Police have arrested three men to assist in investigations into the open sale of ketum water at the Paka Rest and Service (R&R) area yesterday. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairuddin said the suspects, aged between 16 and 32, were arrested during an inspection at the Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Stadium (SSMZA) slip road area near Gong Badak in Kuala Nerus at 7.44pm. “Initial investigations found the ketum water is believed to have been brought into Terengganu for their use throughout their stay here.

items.title: Right after saying ‘I do’, this Gen Z bride in Negeri Sembilan says ‘I vote’
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Amid the excitement of her wedding day, a bride made an unforgettable stop at a polling station, arriving in a striking red traditional bridal outfit to cast her ballot in the Negeri Sembilan state election. Marketing officer Noor Farzana Masnoor, 26, was accompanied by her husband, Luqman Adam Sudirman, 27, as she voted at the Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) Ladang Kubang polling centre in Labu for the Labu constituency. — Bernama

items.title: (Unofficial) Negeri Sembilan polls: ‘PBN’ to form state govt, sets sights on Melaka next
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid has thanked voters and supporters for giving his coalition and Perikatan Nasional the mandate to form the next Negeri Sembilan state government. Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki is claiming victory for the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional pact in the Negeri Sembilan, saying the two have unofficially secured 25 seats from the 36 being contested in today’s state election. Asyraf said the two will jointly form the next state government.

items.title: Counting begins for nearly 12,000 postal ballots as Negeri Sembilan polls enter final stretch
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Postal vote counting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election began at 5pm today. Approximately 12,000 postal ballots are being counted. On 20 July, EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said a total of 13,263 postal ballots had been issued to eligible voters for the state election.

items.title: Merdeka Center: Pakatan’s eight-year track record could matter more than shifting alliances in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) ability to retain voter support in the Negeri Sembilan state election will hinge on whether its eight-year administration has convinced voters that its performance outweighs shifting political alliances. Merdeka Centre programme director Ibrahim Suffian said the state election would indicate whether voters continued to value governance and stability, given that PH has governed Negeri Sembilan since 2018 without any major administrative crises or controversies. While national political developments would inevitably shape voter sentiment, Ibrahim said the state government’s own track record would remain an important consideration at the ballot box.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan voter turnout climbs to 65.38pc by 4pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voter turnout in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election reached 65.38 per cent, with 562,133 of the 859,760 registered voters having cast their ballots as of 4 pm. The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, reported that the Kota state constituency recorded the highest turnout so far at 72.1 per cent, closely followed by Seri Menanti and Labu at 70.9 per cent each. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Mixing politics with business destroys parties, Sanusi warns PAS members against project‑seeking donors
items.summary: GERIK, Aug 1 — PAS has reminded its members to steer clear of business figures seeking to approach the party solely to secure projects without following proper procedures. PAS election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said such practices could damage the party’s internal ecosystem, especially when business entities began demanding projects and bypassing due process, Berita Harian (BH) reported today. When asked whether the Tabung Haji RCI findings might affect cooperation between Barisan Nasional and PAS, Sanusi said the matters raised in the report had no link to PAS.

items.title: Stakeholder feedback crucial in Tabung Haji Act amendments, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1—Engagement sessions with stakeholders are currently underway to gather feedback on the proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535), as recommended by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the move aims to strengthen the legal framework and overall management of the pilgrimage fund board, Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). “We have already held engagement sessions with stakeholders.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — The Meteorological Department has issued a thunderstorm warning for several states, with heavy rain and strong winds expected until 7pm today. The alert covers districts in Perak (Manjung, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Kampar, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Batang Padang and Muallim), Kelantan (Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Bachok, Machang and Pasir Puteh), Terengganu (Kuala Nerus, Hulu Terengganu, Kuala Terengganu, Marang, Dungun and Kemaman), Pahang (Raub, Bentong, Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin), as well as Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The latest warning was issued at 3.45pm today.

items.title: Selangor Education Department offers support following Hulu Selangor teacher’s death, police probe ongoing
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 1 — The Selangor Education Department has deployed psychosocial support to a Hulu Selangor school after a teacher was found dead yesterday. In a statement, JPN Selangor said full cooperation was being given to police investigating the case. It added that priority was being placed on ensuring the victim’s family received the best possible assistance, Harian Metro reported.

items.title: Tengku Permaisuri Selangor decries animal abuse, calls for stronger enforcement and harsher penalties
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 1 — Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin has voiced deep concern over continuing cases of cruelty towards pets and stray animals, particularly dogs and cats, which have recently gone viral. As Royal Patron of the Stray Free Selangor initiative under SPCA Selangor, Her Highness said acts of abuse, injury or killing not only contravene the law but also reflect society’s failure to uphold compassion and humanity. Her Highness said offenders must be investigated thoroughly and face appropriate legal action, including if the acts are committed by enforcement officers.

items.title: EC: Over half of Negeri Sembilan voters turn out by 2pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1— As of 2 pm, 51.58 per cent, or 443,461 of the 859,760 registered voters, had cast their ballots in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. Based on a Facebook post by the Election Commission (EC), the Seri Menanti state constituency recorded the highest voter turnout so far at 57.6 per cent, followed closely by Senaling at 57.2 per cent and Kota at 56.9 per cent. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: IGP says Sanusi case under investigation, police to obtain Kedah MB’s statement
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police will record a statement from Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks he allegedly made touching on racial issues during a recent political ceramah in Jempol. According to Berita Harian , Inspector‑General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the case involving Sanusi remained under investigation. “This matter is still under investigation.

items.title: IGP: 92 reports received, 24 investigation papers opened pertaining to Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police received 92 reports and opened 24 investigation papers throughout the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, which ended at midnight last night. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said most of the reported offences involved minor cases linked to supporters or party members, while four reports on alleged cash handouts to voters were still under investigation. To date, there have been no police reports directly involving candidates, while the overall election process across the 36 state seats has proceeded smoothly and safely,” he said.

items.title: Bukit Aman awaits Indonesian details after Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta airport
items.summary: Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police are awaiting further details from their counterparts before determining the next course of action, the New Straits Times (NST) reported. Hussein told NST that investigators also wanted to determine how many times the suspect might have carried out similar operations and whether he was part of a wider network. Investigators are also examining how the suspect allegedly managed to pass through airport security in Malaysia before departing for Indonesia.

items.title: ‘Shared responsibility’: Hannah Yeoh urges public to help maintain cleanliness during Putrajaya National Day celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 1 — Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she does not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering. “Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish.

items.title: Police tighten security at Negeri Sembilan palace, state offices ahead of poll results
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police will tighten security at key locations, including the Istana of the Yang di Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and state government offices, to prevent any untoward incidents when the Negeri Sembilan state election results are announced later tonight. Inspector General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said there was a possibility that certain quarters might attempt to stir tensions if dissatisfied with the outcome, Sinar Harian reported. Mohd Khalid was speaking to reporters after visiting the polling centre at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan King George V here today.

items.title: Chief Justice heads Pahang state honours list
items.summary: Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah. Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and state government leaders were also in attendance. Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Sri Setia Al-Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAAS) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri Setia.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan confirms two Undang appointments, declares three other claimants invalid
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has formally recognised two newly installed Undang and declared three individuals who claimed the titles of Undang Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu as never having held those positions lawfully. Muhammad Faris Johari was formerly recognised as the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong, while Raja Hassan Ab Hamid’s appointment as Undang Luak Rembau was also affirmed under adat. The DKU also noted that the position of the position of Undang for Sungei Ujong is now vacant after the previous holder, Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, was removed according to adat effective 30 July 2026.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan election sees 37pc voter turnout by noon
items.summary: The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, said the Juasseh constituency recorded the highest voter turnout so far at 43.5 per cent, followed by Chennah (43.4 per cent) and Senaling (42.8 per cent). The Lukut constituency recorded the lowest turnout at about 32.1 per cent. For comparison, voter turnout at the same time during the 15th Negeri Sembilan state election stood at 35.44 per cent, or 297,024 of the 838,200 registered voters.
